newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cash coffee buying slow, industry covered.
newsitem.headline: German cash coffee buying slow, industry covered.

text.p: German cash coffee markets look set to remain lacklustre in August, with roasters well covered and consumption down in the summer season, traders said on Tuesday.
"The industry has built stocks to last for another two months and there is no interest in buying against New York September arabicas at their high premium," one said.
"If there is any buying to speak of, it focuses on Jan-March 1998 Brazils and Centrals or spot robustas."
Nov/Dec Brazils were sold in recent weeks.
Physical coffee prices followed swings on New York arabica futures although Monday's rises were put down to a speculative squeeze by merchants rather than actual shortages.
Traders said U.S. roasters were less well covered than their European counterparts but supply was still comfortable.
The mild winter in Brazil and loss of investor interest in coffee should weigh down futures rather than stabilise the nearby months, they said.
Retail markets were merely ticking over as roasters' price increases were working their way through but consumers were shunning coffee, having hoarded supplies in the spring.
Central American spot arabicas cost around $220-230 per 50 kg fob, while Brazils for Sept shipment were at around $170 and Colombians at $195.
